heroHeadline: Day 705: Sheinbaum Closes 10-State Report Tour in Monterrey and Saltillo as Trump Dismisses Mexico's Exports as 'Tamales and Tomatoes'
heroSubtitle: September 6, 2026 marks Day 705 of Claudia Sheinbaum's presidency. She closed the four-day, ten-state leg of her Second Government Report tour with stops in Monterrey, Nuevo León and Saltillo, Coahuila, touting the 396km Saltillo-Nuevo Laredo passenger rail line, highway modernization, and a new regional IMSS hospital. The tour swung through Colima, Jalisco and Nayarit on September 5, where protesters opposing the Port of Manzanillo's Cuyutlán expansion interrupted Sheinbaum's remarks — she called it provocation — and where she accused former president Vicente Fox and PRI leader Alejandro "Alito" Moreno, after their September 4 meeting, of wanting to "return to the past of corruption and privileges." Also on September 4, President Trump told reporters Mexico has "nothing we need" beyond "tamales picantes, tomates," citing a $195 billion trade deficit, though he said he would not curtail trade given his rapport with Sheinbaum; she responded that Mexico maintains permanent dialogue with Washington and expects an understanding. That followed the same day's Security Cabinet briefing in Zacatecas on the August 30 Ojocaliente car bomb (200kg of explosives, three detained) and Harfuch's confirmation of an active U.S. extradition order against CJNG leader Juan Carlos Valencia González.
